summary: CCC-era 1934 lookout on Inskip Hill in Tehama County with a steel tower and a 1974 cab; the 2024 Park Fire damaged outbuildings and a rebuild was planned for 2025.

facts.design: USFS L-801 tower; cab replaced in 1974 with a 732-6A style cab

access.note: Sources conflict. The Register, citing a note dated October 1991, says the station is accessible to the public, 4.5 miles from the nearest paved road. Peakbagging says it is on private land. A CAL FIRE reconstruction is planned for 2025; its completion is unconfirmed. Check with CAL FIRE before going.

visit.trail_note: The Register says the station is 4.5 miles from the nearest paved road. Peakbagging says it is on private land. Do not climb the tower.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE), Tehama-Glenn Unit

events.note: Original CCC-era lookout built for the Forest Service; tower and garage built by CCC crews.
Newspaper item (Oroville Mercury, June 22, 1935, as transcribed): a 40-foot steel tower carrying the lookout, manned by Victor Mentink.
Hubert Grissom, lookout (Lassen Advocate item, June 21, 1937, as transcribed).
Lassen National Forest staffed or operated the site until 1958.
Tower and immediate property quit claimed to CDF.
A 13,000-acre fire near Red Bluff knocked out power lines to the tower, the main radio relay point for local law enforcement (Nevada State Journal item, August 21, 1973, as transcribed).
BC-3 cab replaced with a 732-6A style cab. The original cab (BC-301) had been destroyed by fire; the date of the fire is not given.
Date registered per the Register: October 28, 2019.
Park Fire damaged the garage, electrical infrastructure and privy. The lookout itself survived, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association's August 2024 post.
CAL FIRE Notice of Exemption for the Inskip Lookout Reconstruction Project, received December 17, 2024. Phase III planned for spring-summer 2025; completion not confirmed in the sources read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Park Fire damaged the garage, electrical infrastructure and privy, and the 2024 CAL FIRE notice describes replacing them. The notice does not list the tower as damaged, and the Forest Fire Lookout Association says the lookout survived the fire.

sources.title: Forest Fire Lookout Association Instagram post, August 31, 2024

notes_for_editor: Access conflict: the NHLR's October 1991 note says accessible to the public; Peakbagging says private land. Settle before the access note is treated as final. Tower date: the 1935 newspaper already describes a 40-foot steel tower; Peakbagging says the steel tower replaced the 1934 lookout around 1975; the Register dates the 1974 cab change. Staffing: Peakbagging says a Forest Service employee staffs it in fire season; the FFLA post says it is not normally staffed by CAL FIRE; no source gives a current staffing date (as_of is undated). Agency naming: the Register and the 2024 notice say CAL FIRE; the Register's 1958 and 1971 entries show the Forest Service and CDF roles. The FFLA list's register numbers for Inskip and Iaqua Buttes do not match the NHLR detail pages. The record's agency string has a stray double bracket ('TGU))'). Completion of the 2025 rebuild is unverified.
